newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 25.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:

* News Corp and EchoStar Communications are combining their direct satellite businesses to offer a subscription television service in the United States, posing a challenge to the nation's cable providers.

* The Catera by General Motors' Cadillac is the latest product by the company to lure younger customers. Although sales of the $30,000 vehicle are picking up, some industry experts say Cadillac's condition remains precarious.
* Shares of PPL Therapeutics Plc rose 16.4 percent after a British scientist's announcement that he successfully cloned a sheep in collaboration with the Scottish company.

* Some traders either knew bad news was coming or got very lucky in the days before Scholastic Inc released negative news. Volume in the company's stock was low before the announcement, but volume in put options on the stock at the Chicago Board Options Exchange was far above average.
* Applied Magnetics made an unsolicited offer for Read-Rite for about $1.76 billion in stock, saying talks for a friendly combination with the computer disk head supplier had stalled.
* American Electric Power and Public Service Co of Colorado agreed to acquire Britain's Yorkshire Electricity for $2.43 billion.
* Chubb Corp agreed to sell its life insurance business to Jefferson-Pilot, and ReliaStar Financial said it would buy Security-Connecticut for $413 million.
* SmithKline Beecham agreed to pay the U.S. Government $325 million to settle charges it overcharged Medicare for patient services.

* Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical Industries agreed to acquire Japan's Green Cross Corp, a company facing $195 million in payments to settle with hemophiliacs infected with HIV from its blood-clotting products.
* Technology stocks soared, and the Dow industrials rose 76.58 to 7,008.20.
* The yield on the 30-year Treasury rose to 6.65 percent from 6.64 percent.
* Richard Lesher, president of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, said he is resigning.
* The Army Times Publishing Co, a family-owned business that publishes a weekly newspaper of the U.S. Army, is for sale and has hired Furman Selz.
* Time Warner's Time Inc is planning to launch an Asian edition of Money magazine.
* Britain's Thorn Plc is closing 90 Radio Rentals stores and cutting 360 jobs to cut costs as sales slump.
* Russia said its nuclear weapons establishment has obtained an IBM supercomputer despite U.S. export controls.
* The Supreme Court will review a lower-court ruling that limits the membership of federally chartered credit unions.

* The government said high doses of birth control pills taken soon after unprotected sex are a means of preventing pregnancy, and it published dosages for brands made by Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories, a unit of American Home Products, and Berlex Laboratories, a subsidiary of Schering.
